runtime_gate.reason: Existing canonical F-host shared-runner heartbeat remains stale and height_difference_2 guarded operator recovery remains unexecuted.

score_basis: Non-statistical internal evidence-quality score based on BGS/UKRI and government mining/minerals guidance, with susceptibility mapping explicitly separated from site investigation, geotechnical design and parcel-specific ground conditions.

sources.label: BGS GeoSure
sources.fact: National 1:50,000 susceptibility datasets cover six natural ground-movement themes and support planning decisions; they are hazard susceptibility, not site-specific risk certification.

sources.label: BGS GeoSure shrink-swell
sources.fact: 1:50,000 shrink-swell susceptibility is derived from geological and engineering information; detailed local investigation may still be required.

sources.label: BGS GeoSure shrink-swell 3D London and Thames Valley
sources.fact: London/Thames Valley product maps A-E shrink-swell susceptibility in 3D down to 20m intervals; it remains regional hazard evidence.

sources.label: BGS GeoClimate Shrink-Swell
sources.fact: 2026 BGS product combines GeoSure geology with climate projections to model future shrink-swell susceptibility; projections are not parcel foundation design.

sources.label: BGS GeoSure compressible ground
sources.fact: Maps potential compressible-ground hazard from superficial/bedrock deposits; loading and groundwater change can affect settlement.

sources.label: BGS GeoSure collapsible deposits
sources.fact: Maps potential collapsible-deposit hazard at 1:50,000; specialist advice may be needed where susceptibility is material.

sources.label: BGS GeoSure running sand
sources.fact: Maps potential running-sand hazard; water flow can fluidise loose sandy layers and affect support.

sources.label: BGS GeoSure soluble rocks
sources.fact: Maps dissolution/subsidence susceptibility where soluble rocks can form cavities; site-specific assessment remains necessary.

sources.label: BGS GeoSure landslides
sources.fact: Susceptibility mapping combines geology, slope and landslide evidence; BGS explicitly states it does not show risk or timing.

sources.label: BGS National Landslide Database
sources.fact: Contains more than 17,000 reported landslide records across Great Britain; event records are not a parcel geotechnical investigation.

sources.label: Mining Remediation Authority Coal Mining Risk Assessment guidance
sources.fact: Development High Risk Area proposals generally require a Coal Mining Risk Assessment; mine-entry locations may require intrusive investigation.

sources.label: GOV.UK Minerals planning guidance
sources.fact: Mineral Safeguarding Areas protect resources from unnecessary sterilisation but do not create a presumption that minerals will be worked.

examples.result: GeoSure susceptibility class is not converted to predicted foundation cost or parcel viability.
London shrink-swell 3D evidence is regional/local hazard context and not a borehole or laboratory result.
GeoClimate projection is future susceptibility evidence, not current observed ground movement.
Landslide susceptibility is not probability/timing; BGS explicitly separates susceptibility from risk.
Coal Development High Risk Area status triggers assessment requirements but does not prove a mine feature beneath a parcel.
Low-risk coalfield status is not negative proof of all subsurface hazards.
Mineral Safeguarding Area designation is not a presumption of extraction or development refusal.
No ground/mineral promotion occurs without exact site geometry plus current geotechnical/mining evidence where relevant.
